_reviewProof: 2026-08-01: proof of review moved from hand-written marker files to the RECORDED ledger. A marker is a separate act of writing performed by the party being audited â€” twelve such writes were flagged as forged in Butlery on 2026-08-01, and every stricter spelling of the assertion (name the file, pin the sha, list what you read) was still an assertion. In ledger mode a PostToolUse hook records which reviewer read which bytes and a SubagentStop hook records the verdict it ended on; nothing is hand-writable, and a later fix silently un-proves the file it touched. This repo's four agents already pinned shas honestly, so this is a hardening rather than a repair. All four carry the two rules it depends on: open files with Read, and end on REVIEW-VERDICT: pass|fail (N blocking).

reviewGates._note2: 2026-08-08: added `^\.github/(workflows|actions)/`. Before this, NO gate in this repo covered the release path at all — a change to `deploy.yml` (which builds and deploys production), `preview.yml`, `ci.yml` or `secret-scan.yml` reached zero reviewers. Meanwhile `.claude/rules/deployment.md` already lists `.github/workflows/**` in its auto-load `paths:`, so the repo's own prose treated it as load-bearing while the automated half — the one that actually runs — did not. Two sources, opposite answers, and the automated one wins by default. Found by sweeping all three repos on 2026-08-08 after the same gap was fixed in Synat (BIN-820), where the identical widening (BIN-667) had already been made and this repo never got it. These are REGEXES, not globs: a literal `.github/workflows/**` throws `Nothing to repeat` at `new RegExp()`. `actions` is in the alternation even though this repo has no `.github/actions/` yet — Synat learned that gating only `workflows/` exempts logic the moment anything is extracted into a composite action (BIN-666/667), and the cheap time to cover it is before that move, not after.
reviewGates._note3: 2026-08-09, BIN-830: added the pattern matching exactly docs/org/route.mjs, docs/org/route.test.mjs, scripts/check-workflow-map.mjs and scripts/check-workflow-map.test.mjs. BIN-805 (24f6612) taught the ADVISING router (docs/org/route.mjs, TOOLING_CODE_FILES) that the router and the workflow-map linter ARE code; this BLOCKING gate was never widened to match, so a commit touching only route.mjs reached zero reviewers -- the self-clearing hole the ticket was filed about. Two lists decide who reviews a change and widening one never widens the other; keep them identical and grow both in the same commit. Deliberately scoped to those four paths and NOT to docs/**/*.mjs + scripts/**/*.mjs as the ticket text proposed: the narrow list is Malin's 2026-08-08 call (alternative (a)), and route.mjs carries a golden selftest asserting scripts/gen-app-icons.mjs stays tier skip -- a broad glob would make the blocking gate contradict a decided routing. Same shape as cd8c59e (.github/). Widening only; nothing was removed.
reviewGates._note4: 2026-08-12, BIN-851: added THIS FILE and .claude/rules/accepted-deviations.md. BIN-830 one level up, and that level decides all the others: no gate pattern here could match `.claude/shared-plugin.json`, so a commit that DELETES a reviewer pattern reached zero reviewers and convened no panel -- the gate could disarm itself unwitnessed. accepted-deviations.md is in for the mirror-image reason: it decides what a reviewer is forbidden to flag, so appending to it silently retires a finding class. Deliberately NOT `^\.claude/rules/.*\.md$` as the ticket's second criterion floated: lessons-digest.md is appended by the fold-back step of every single sprint close-out, and putting the integration reviewer in that path would gate routine bookkeeping on a review -- the same narrow-over-broad call Malin made for BIN-830. Also added to docs/role-responsibilities.md Sec 25 (Engineering Manager / Release Manager owns the process and the quality gates), so the ADVISING router stops answering `skip` for this file; both lists moved in one commit, per the BIN-830 lesson. Widening only; nothing was removed.
reviewGates._note5: 2026-08-12, BIN-864 + BIN-873: added `gen-ownership-map` and `check-public-env` to the same alternation. Both routed `skip` with zero reviewers at bfb82f4, so a commit touching either alone reached nobody. check-public-env.mjs is the guard that exists BECAUSE NEXT_PUBLIC_FCM_VAPID_KEY was never wired into the production build for three months (BIN-849) -- push registered zero devices while CI and deploy stayed green; the watchman against silent breakage was itself unwatched. gen-ownership-map.mjs computes ownership-map.json (the input to who-owns-what) and, since bfb82f4, is the source of a check that fails `npm test` and therefore deploy.yml. Kept as a narrow alternation rather than `scripts/**/*.mjs` + `docs/**/*.mjs`: Malin's 2026-08-08 call, alternative (a), unchanged. #25 Engineering Manager's blind critique SUPPORTED this with conditions and noted the real point -- all four widenings of this gate have been REACTIVE, found by a reviewer or an incident. The trigger to stop patching the regex and build a mechanical symmetry check instead is a third hole found the same way. CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (BIN-880, criterion 4): this sentence originally ended 'filed as its own ticket rather than done here', in the past tense, and no such ticket existed on 2026-08-12 -- the integration review caught it the next day. The real ticket is BIN-880, filed 2026-08-13, and the check it asked for now exists as docs/org/gate-symmetry.test.mjs. Widening only; nothing was removed.
reviewGates._note6: 2026-08-13, BIN-869: added the reviewers' own four instruction files and the three hooks. Same hole as _note4 one file away -- editing what a reviewer is TOLD to look for disarms a gate exactly as effectively as deleting its pattern, and both routed `skip` and matched nothing. The `*.knowledge.md` / `*.knowledge.archive.md` siblings are DELIBERATELY excluded: the reviewers append to those on every ledger run, so gating them would put routine bookkeeping behind a review -- the same call Malin made for lessons-digest.md in _note4. The hooks are named individually rather than `.claude/hooks/**` for the same narrow-over-broad reason as BIN-830/851/864/873 (Malin's 2026-08-08 call, alternative (a)). route.mjs and gen-ownership-map.mjs were already covered by _note3/_note5; what BIN-869 adds for them is the OWNERSHIP half in docs/role-responsibilities.md Sec 25, not a gate pattern -- the ticket's own evidence bullet claiming gen-ownership-map.mjs reached no gate was stale as of 7051a98 and is corrected on the ticket. This is the FOURTH reactive widening; the mechanical ownership-vs-gate symmetry check that _note5 named as the trigger was NOT done here. CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (BIN-880, criterion 4): as written on 2026-08-13 this sentence said that check 'is BIN-880, filed 2026-08-13' while the ticket was still being written -- the same past tense _note5 was corrected for, one day later. BIN-880 exists now and shipped on 2026-08-16 as docs/org/gate-symmetry.test.mjs, so a sixth widening of this alternation is meant to be found by a red test rather than by a reviewer. Widening only; nothing was removed.
reviewGates._note7: 2026-08-16, BIN-880: the FIFTH widening, and the last one that should ever be found by hand -- it ships together with docs/org/gate-symmetry.test.mjs, which walks every git-tracked path and fails when the ADVISING side (docs/org/route.mjs + docs/org/ownership-map.json) and this BLOCKING list disagree about it. Precisely: it fails when an owned or high-stakes code path reaches ZERO reviewers here, not when it loses a PARTICULAR one -- deleting `^functions/` or `^src/lib/firebase/` leaves those files matched by `\.(ts|tsx)$` above and stays green. That limit is stated in the check's own header; the rules count reviewers, they do not identify them. The six paths added here are exactly what that check found on its first run, not a guess: CLAUDE.md and .github/dependabot.yml were the only two of role #25's fifteen owned paths reaching zero reviewers (CLAUDE.md is the paragraph telling every agent how to route a change and when to convene a panel -- BIN-869 edited it and nothing fired); firebase.json, next.config.mjs and src/app/globals.css are owned CODE that no gate stopped (hosting rewrites + the rules/indexes file mapping, the build config, and the entire Direction H token set -- a CSS-only commit reached nobody at all); gate-symmetry.test.mjs joins the existing alternation because a check that can be weakened unreviewed is the hole BIN-869 closed one file over. Two more asymmetries were fixed on the ROUTER side instead, which adds no blocking obligation: vitest.rules.config.ts and vitest.setup.ts were already stopped by this gate while the router called them skip. Three remain as NAMED exceptions with a reason each in gate-symmetry.test.mjs (functions/.gitignore, scripts/scripts-self-tests-present.test.mjs, .github/workflows/secret-scan.yml) -- a silence would have been the sixth hole. Still exact paths rather than globs: Malin's narrow-over-broad call, 2026-08-08, alternative (a), unchanged. Widening only; nothing was removed.
